This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: John Henry Holliday was born on August 14, 1851, in Griffin, Georgia. [D]
In 1866 Holliday's mother died of tuberculosis. [D]
He enrolled at the Pennsylvania College of Dental Surgery in 1870 and graduated in 1872, then practiced dentistry in Atlanta before opening his own practice in Griffin. [D]

Shortly after beginning his career as a dentist in Atlanta he developed a bad cough; doctors diagnosed tuberculosis and advised a move to a more arid climate. He developed chronic pulmonary tuberculosis. [D]
He was diagnosed with tuberculosis in 1873 and moved west for a healthier, drier climate, arriving in Dallas, Texas, in September 1873. [D]
He made his living at the card tables, aggravating his tuberculosis with heavy drinking and late nights. [D]

text.paragraph: 1 later historical claim is omitted because it describes events after the index age. See the teaching note.

Plays poker for money several nights a week; up late most nights [S]
No tobacco or other drug use; no travel outside the country; no incarceration or homelessness [S]

text.paragraph: No medications started by this date.

Positive for the concerns in the history of present illness. Alert, sharp, and dryly humorous; organized thought; no signs of intoxication or withdrawal. Mood worried about his work and his health; PHQ-9 6; no thoughts of suicide or self-harm. No other systems reported as affected in this synthetic episode. [S]

Structured safety assessment: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent, access to means reviewed: yes. Routine outpatient care. A new serious diagnosis, isolation, and heavy drinking can raise suicide risk, so safety is reviewed at every visit. He saved the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline in his phone. No firearm in the home. Alcohol use disorder, mild, with binge drinking: active, confirmed [S]

Infectious diseases consultation to confirm the regimen and plan monitoring for cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis in a man who drinks heavily. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); Updates on the Treatment of Drug-Susceptible and Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis: An Official ATS/CDC/ERS/IDSA Clinical Practice Guideline (2025) [S]

Standard treatment: isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for eight weeks, then isoniazid and rifampin for eighteen weeks, by video-observed therapy with the health department, with pyridoxine. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016) [S]

Monitoring: monthly symptom and weight check, sputum smear and culture monthly until two consecutive cultures are negative, liver tests at two weeks and monthly because of alcohol, and vision checks while on ethambutol. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); An official ATS statement: hepatotoxicity of antituberculosis therapy (2006) [S]

Public health: same-day report to the local health department, home isolation until noninfectious, and a contact investigation of his household, coworkers, and patients led by the health department. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); Guidelines for the investigation of contacts of persons with infectious tuberculosis: recommendations from the National Tuberculosis Controllers Association and CDC (2005) [S]

Alcohol care: brief intervention at diagnosis, a goal of no alcohol during treatment, counseling with a substance-use counselor, medication offered, AUDIT-C at each visit, and a safety review with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at every visit. Guideline: Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions (2018); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Substance Use Disorders (2021); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024) [S]
